Childhood mortality rates

Source: R/rates.R
bdhs_mortality.Rd

Computes neonatal (NNMR), postneonatal (PNNMR), infant (IMR), child (CMR, 4q1) and under-five (U5MR) mortality rates per 1,000 live births with the DHS synthetic cohort life-table method: probabilities of dying are estimated for the age segments 0, 1-2, 3-5, 6-11, 12-23, 24-35, 36-47 and 48-59 months from the births and deaths in the reference period, counting half of the exposure (and deaths) of cohorts only partly exposed at the start of the period, and half of the exposure of cohorts partly exposed at its end. Standard errors use the DHS jackknife over clusters.

Usage

bdhs_mortality(
  data,
  period = 5,
  rates = c("nnmr", "pnnmr", "imr", "cmr", "u5mr"),
  by = NULL,
  se = TRUE,
  level = 0.95,
  survey = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A births recode (BR, one row per birth with b3, b7) or a women's recode (IR, wide birth history b3_01, b7_01, ...), with v008, v005 and v021.

period

Length of the reference period in years before the interview (DHS standard: 5; 10 for subgroups).

rates

Which rates to return.

by

Optional character vector of grouping variables (birth- or woman-level).

se

If TRUE (default), compute jackknife standard errors and confidence intervals.

level

Confidence level.

survey

Optional survey reference, overriding detection.

Value

A tibble with columns survey_id, the by variables, indicator, estimate (per 1,000 live births), se, ci_low, ci_high, n_births (unweighted births contributing to the rates), n_deaths, n_psu and period (years).

See also

bdhs_fertility(), bdhs_estimate()

Examples

br <- bdhs_simulate(2017, "BR")
bdhs_mortality(br, se = FALSE)
#> # A tibble: 5 × 10
#>   survey_id indicator estimate    se ci_low ci_high n_births n_deaths n_psu
#>   <chr>     <chr>        <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl>   <dbl>    <int>    <int> <int>
#> 1 BD2017DHS nnmr          33.8    NA     NA      NA      608       25    40
#> 2 BD2017DHS pnnmr         27.7    NA     NA      NA      608       25    40
#> 3 BD2017DHS imr           61.5    NA     NA      NA      608       25    40
#> 4 BD2017DHS cmr           20.2    NA     NA      NA      608       25    40
#> 5 BD2017DHS u5mr          80.5    NA     NA      NA      608       25    40
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: period <dbl>
bdhs_mortality(br, period = 10, rates = c("imr", "u5mr"), by = "v025")
#> # A tibble: 4 × 11
#>   survey_id v025  indicator estimate    se ci_low ci_high n_births n_deaths
#>   <chr>     <fct> <chr>        <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl>   <dbl>    <int>    <int>
#> 1 BD2017DHS urban imr           57.4  14.1   29.8    85.1      453       24
#> 2 BD2017DHS urban u5mr          75.9  15.8   44.8   107.       453       24
#> 3 BD2017DHS rural imr           53.5  11.9   30.2    76.8      538       24
#> 4 BD2017DHS rural u5mr          74.2  16.7   41.5   107.       538       24
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: n_psu <int>, period <dbl>
